summary.authors: K Hayama, S D Mohanty, M Rakhmanov, S Desai
summary.executive_summary: This paper introduces RIDGE, a novel data analysis pipeline designed specifically for triggered gravitational wave (GW) burst searches. Unlike all-sky blind searches, triggered searches benefit from prior astronomical information (e.g., sky location from Gamma-ray Bursts) and smaller data volumes, allowing for computationally intensive algorithms. The authors describe a pipeline that combines advanced data conditioning—using running median noise floor estimation and MBLT line removal—with a coherent network detection statistic based on regularized maximum likelihood. Specifically, the pipeline achieves a detection probability of approximately 62% for a signal with an amplitude of $5 \times 10^{-22} \text{ Hz}^{-1/2}$ at a false alarm rate of $2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ Hz}$. Executive Summary
This paper introduces RIDGE, a novel data analysis pipeline designed specifically for triggered gravitational wave (GW) burst searches. Unlike all-sky blind searches, triggered searches benefit from prior astronomical information (e.g., sky location from Gamma-ray Bursts) and smaller data volumes, allowing for computationally intensive algorithms. The authors describe a pipeline that combines advanced data conditioning—using running median noise floor estimation and MBLT line removal—with a coherent network detection statistic based on regularized maximum likelihood. Simulations using a network of LIGO and Virgo detectors demonstrate that the proposed radial statistic ($R_{rad}$) significantly outperforms a naive maximum/minimum statistic ($R_{mm}$). Specifically, the pipeline achieves a detection probability of approximately 62% for a signal with an amplitude of $5 \times 10^{-22} \text{ Hz}^{-1/2}$ at a false alarm rate of $2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ Hz}$. The study highlights the importance of utilizing full sky-map information and suggests that RIDGE provides a robust, independent check for existing analysis methods.

Research Context
Triggered searches differ fundamentally from blind all-sky searches. Prior information like sky location guides the analysis. Small data volumes allow expensive algorithms. Blind searches are limited by computational resources. Existing pipelines lack robust handling of non-stationarity.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can new algorithms improve sensitivity in triggered searches? Does incorporating full sky-map information improve detection? Will regularized maximum likelihood outperform hard constraints? Can triggered searches achieve higher sensitivity than un-triggered ones? Is the radial statistic superior to the max/min statistic?

Methodological Details
The study uses simulated noise and signals. The network includes H1, L1, H2, and V1 detectors. Noise PSDs approximate design sensitivity curves. Artifacts include sinusoids at specific frequencies. Injected signals are sine-Gaussian with Q=9. Signal amplitudes range from 3e-22 to 7e-22 Hz^-1/2. Data conditioning uses a two-step process. Noise floor is estimated via running median. Whitening uses FIR filters trained on 2 seconds. Line removal uses the MBLT method. Sky maps are generated in 0.5 sec segments. Integration time is larger than the 40 msec signal duration.

Procedures And Architectures
The pipeline is written mostly in matlab. Data conditioning mitigates instrumental artifacts. Running median rejects outliers like power line interference. Whitening filter transfer function is 1/sqrt(S(f)). Regularization solves the ill-posed inversion problem. The algorithm outputs a likelihood sky-map S(theta, phi). Two detection statistics are compared: Rmm and Rrad. Rrad is the radial distance in scaled space. Simulations used 3000 seconds of Gaussian noise. Four independent realizations of white noise were used.

Key Results
Rrad outperforms Rmm in detection capability. Detection probability is 62% for hrss = 5e-22. False alarm rate is 1 event per 50 seconds. ROC curves show clear separation for different hrss. Rrad incorporates full sky-map information. Performance estimates are lower bounds. Signal injection location was GRB060813. Sampling frequency was 16384 Hz. Filter delays are known because filters are FIR. Ridge provides an independent check for other pipelines.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Full sky-map statistics are required for triggered searches. Judicious choice of statistic is definitely required. Ridge offers a platform for trying out new regulators. The pipeline reconstructs waveforms at arbitrary sky locations. Ridge should be applied to real triggered events. The radial statistic utilizes ensemble averages. Regularization handles direction-dependent antenna patterns. The hard constraint is a limit of infinite gain.

Contradictions And Limitations
Non-stationarity in noise floor creates discrepancies. Integration time is much larger than signal duration. Filter delays have not been removed in the current version. More effective full sky-map statistics can be derived. The study relies on simulated data. Line removal requires manual finding of carrier frequency. The code details are not described in the paper. Only two detector networks were simulated.

Claims
The RIDGE pipeline significantly improves detection sensitivity for triggered searches compared to standard methods. Rrad statistics performs better than Rmm. 62% detection probability at low false alarm rate. Judicious choice of statistic is required. Performance estimates are lower bounds. Integration time is larger than signal duration. Ridge provides an independent check. Platform for new regulators.
Regularized maximum likelihood is superior to hard constraint methods for network analysis. Hard constraint is limit of infinite gain. Regularization solves ill-posed inversion. Theoretical aspects are well understood. Better waveform reconstruction.

Data And Code Availability
Code is written in matlab but details are not provided. Code details are not described in this paper.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Running median rejects outliers effectively. Line removal does not affect signals. Transient signals appear as outliers.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows PSD and running median estimate. Figure 2 shows spectrograms before and after line removal. Figure 3 shows sky-maps for noise and signal cases. Figure 4 shows PSDs of simulated detector noise. Figure 5 shows detector responses to injection signal. Figure 6 shows ROC curves for Rmm and Rrad.

Three Takeaways
RIDGE pipeline implements regularized maximum likelihood. Rrad statistic outperforms Rmm in simulations. Future work will integrate waveform estimation.
